    Coming Back

    How a pi-durable agent survives a crash, taught one concept at a time

    What this is about

    An agent that runs for minutes or hours will be interrupted: a laptop lid closes, a process crashes, a deploy restarts the server. pi-durable is an agent harness built so that an interruption loses (almost) nothing: the conversation, the running tools and the user's last message all come back after a restart.

    The example

    Lena runs a coding agent on her laptop. Mid-turn, while bash runs the test suite, she closes the lid and the process dies. Each concept follows that turn through one mechanism: how state is stored, how work continues, what happens to the interrupted tool, and why her last message is not sent twice.

    How it progresses

    Five concepts: commits, tasks, tools after a crash, retried submissions, and the limits.

    How this works

    A tutor takes you through 5 concepts in order, one at a time: it explains with an example and a figure, then asks a check question and waits for your answer. Answer in your own words, or ask anything at any point. The outline shows where you are.
